STEP 1 - Scene: A top-down photo of a plate of what looks like scrambled egg whites in white chunks. A second plate at the left edge holds roasted sweet potato and grapes. It is not part of this meal.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The main plate is a square-ish side/dinner plate about 24 cm wide. Its area is roughly 24 x 24 minus the rounded corners, so about 540 cm^2. I'll use about 500 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Scrambled egg white (cooked, soft white chunks). No visible oil or sauce.

STEP 4 - Area: The pile spans roughly 380 px of the 450 px plate width and about 270 px of its height. That is about 1/3 of the plate, or roughly 30% of the area, which is about 150 cm^2.

STEP 5 - Volume: The pieces are fluffy chunks about 2 cm high, so 150 x 2 = 300 ml gross.

STEP 6 - Grams: Egg white pieces are fairly dense, but the pile has gaps. Using a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml gives roughly 180 g. This could be somewhat lower, so I'll use about 170 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked egg white is about 52 kcal/100 g. 170 g x 0.52 = 88 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 170 g of egg white is roughly 5 egg whites. That fits a mound covering a third of a plate.
